title: ROAX record envelope v1
description: Envelope for a record committed under ROAX-CANON/1. Carries EITHER a full record OR a selective disclosure, never both. Normative text: docs/spec/roax-canon-1.md section 11. DRAFT - not frozen.

canon.description: Canonicalization version. Bound into the Merkle root via the domain string in every leaf and every salt (spec sections 8, 7, 12).

hashAlg.description: Hash algorithm, selected per record. ZK-friendly and non-ZK hashes are both first-class (decision B, ruled). Bound TWICE so it cannot be substituted: it is appended to the domain string, which is ASCII 'ROAX-CANON/1/' + hashAlg and sits in every salt preimage and every leaf preimage (spec sections 7, 8, 7.4), AND it is committed inside the root as the reserved leaf roax.hashAlg (spec section 11.2). So two records with identical content and different hashAlg have different roots. CAUTION: only SHA-256 has a construction DEFINED by ROAX-CANON/1. Poseidon-BN254 is REGISTERED but its parameterization - field, rate and capacity, round constants, and the byte-string-to-field-element encoding the byte layouts do not survive without - is NOT yet pinned. A record MUST NOT be issued under Poseidon-BN254 until a revision pins it (spec section 7.4).

recordType.description: Profile identifier, in lowercase reverse-DNS form. Committed inside the root at the reserved path roax.recordType. NORMATIVE: the registry of valid values is docs/profiles/, one document per value, and adding a value REQUIRES adding a profile document declaring at minimum its schemaVersion, its type-map scope and its non-redactable path set (spec section 10.2). The v1 registry is sg.gov.moh.vaccination-healthcert, sg.gov.moh.pdt-healthcert, sg.gov.moh.recovery-healthcert and hl7.fhir.bundle. A pattern rather than an enum, because the registry is extensible by adding a profile document and is not a closed universe; the pattern constrains the FORM only, and a syntactically valid value with no profile document is not a valid record.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the record profile named by recordType. Committed inside the root. Two or three components: the healthcert profiles use two (1.0, 2.0) and hl7.fhir.bundle uses the real FHIR version 4.0.1, which is three.

recordId.description: Stable identifier for this record. Committed inside the root AND folded into every salt preimage (spec section 7.1). MUST be unique per record. Reusing it across a reissuance weakens cross-record unlinkability - see decision D4.

root.description: RFC 9162 Merkle Tree Head over all leaves, lowercase hex, no 0x prefix.

leafCount.description: Total number of leaves in the tree, which is the UNION of the record's own leaves and the reserved roax.* leaves - NOT the record's leaves alone (spec sections 3.3 and 11.2). Six reserved leaves are always emitted (roax.canon, roax.hashAlg, roax.recordType, roax.schemaVersion, roax.recordId, roax.issuer.id) and roax.issuer.keyId adds a seventh when issuer.keyId is present. Required to verify an RFC 9162 inclusion proof, which is bound to (index, tree size), so an implementation that counts only the record produces a leafCount that does not match its own root. The minimum is 7: a record contributing zero leaves of its own MUST be rejected at issuance (spec section 3.3), so the tree is never empty.

issuer.description: Issuer IDENTITY. Committed inside the root at reserved paths (spec section 11.2). Distinct from anchor, which is routing only.

anchor.description: Routing hint ONLY. NEVER authority. Outside the Merkle root, therefore attacker-controlled (spec section 11.3). A verifier MUST re-derive authority from the anchoring layer it is itself configured with, never from these values. No contract set is permanent; these fields are illustrative.

disclosure.description: Present in a DISCLOSED copy only. Mutually exclusive with `record`.

record.description: Present in a FULL copy only. The typed record. A verifier derives every salt from masterSalt and recomputes the root from scratch. Mutually exclusive with `disclosure`. CAUTION: this object carries record numbers in their original JSON form, so the parser requirement of spec section 6.4 applies to the WHOLE ENVELOPE and not only to a bare record. An implementation that reads a full copy through a float-based JSON parser destroys the very literals it is about to recompute the root from (spec section 7.3).

masterSalt.description: The per-record master secret, 32 bytes as lowercase hex. REQUIRED in a full copy and FORBIDDEN in a disclosed copy, enforced by the allOf clauses below (spec section 7.3). A full copy needs it because leafHash needs salt(path), salt(path) needs masterSalt, and the record body carries no per-leaf salts; without it a full copy has no route to any leaf hash and therefore none to the root. It leaks nothing there, because a full copy already discloses every value at every path. A DISCLOSED copy carries only the individual derived salts of the leaves it reveals, because masterSalt would let its holder brute-force every withheld low-entropy leaf. MUST be 32 fresh CSPRNG bytes PER RECORD: reuse lets a holder of one full copy derive the salts of the other record too. A holder downgrading a full copy to a disclosed copy MUST strip this field.

pathSegment.description: One structured path segment. The verifier re-encodes the path from THESE, per spec section 5. The display path is never hashed and MUST NOT be parsed to reconstruct segments.

key.description: Object key. Normalized to NFC before encoding. May be the empty string, which is distinct from an absent segment.

index.description: 0-based array index. MUST be < 2^32; an implementation that cannot represent it MUST error rather than truncate.

segments.description: The structured path. Authoritative for hashing.

displayPath.description: Human-readable form such as a.b[0].c. DISPLAY ONLY. Never hashed, never parsed back into segments (spec section 5.2).

index.description: Leaf index in encodePath order. Together with the envelope's leafCount this binds the RFC 9162 proof to a position.

tag.description: ROAX type tag (spec section 6.1). 0 NULL, 1 BOOL, 2 STRING, 3 INTEGER, 4 DECIMAL, 5 BYTES, 6 EMPTY_ARRAY, 7 EMPTY_OBJECT. MUST come from the type map, never from the JSON literal's syntax (spec section 4).

value.description: The value, in the carrier form for its tag: boolean for BOOL; string for STRING; a canonical numeric STRING for INTEGER and DECIMAL - never a JSON number, because a JSON number would be parsed through a float and destroy precision (spec section 6.4); lowercase hex for BYTES. Absent for NULL, EMPTY_ARRAY and EMPTY_OBJECT. The concrete type is pinned per tag by the allOf conditionals below.

salt.description: The derived salt for this path, 16 bytes as lowercase hex. Disclosing it reveals nothing about any other leaf's salt, because derivation is HMAC (spec section 7.2). The masterSalt itself MUST NEVER appear in a DISCLOSED copy - it would let the verifier derive the salt of every withheld leaf and brute-force the low-entropy ones. It is carried in a FULL copy, where it discloses nothing extra and is required to recompute the root at all (spec section 7.3).

auditPath.description: RFC 9162 section 2.1.3 audit path, root-ward, lowercase hex.

allOf.description: Tags NULL(0), EMPTY_ARRAY(6) and EMPTY_OBJECT(7) carry no value.
INTEGER(3) carries a canonical integer STRING: no leading zeros, -0 normalized to 0 (spec section 6.2).

DECIMAL(4) carries a canonical decimal STRING in positional notation. Trailing zeros in the fraction are SIGNIFICANT and preserved: 0.010 is not 0.01 (FHIR R4 SHALL, spec section 6.2). Exponent notation has already been expanded, so it is not accepted here.
BYTES(5) carries lowercase hex of even length.
A full copy and a disclosed copy are mutually exclusive. A verifier that sees both MUST reject.
Exactly one of them must be present.
A FULL copy MUST carry masterSalt. Without it there is no route from the record to any leaf hash, because leafHash needs salt(path) and salt(path) needs masterSalt (spec section 7.3).

A DISCLOSED copy MUST NOT carry masterSalt. It carries only the per-leaf derived salts of the leaves it reveals; masterSalt would let its holder derive the salt of every withheld leaf (spec section 7.3).

$comment: This schema cannot express two normative requirements, which therefore MUST be enforced in code and are covered by the conformance corpus: (1) the minimum-disclosure floor - each profile declares non-redactable paths that a disclosed copy MUST contain (spec section 10.2); JSON Schema cannot check set membership of decoded path segments against a per-profile list. (2) the reserved-prefix guard - no record-supplied path may begin with 'roax.' (spec section 11.2). See docs/conformance-corpus.md classes 14 and 15.
